archives-brief.text: Welcome back. Two parcels arrived on this machine as zip files, and one of them is locked with a password. Let's open both.

archives-extract.text: Now unpack it. Type unzip, then the file name. If it asks whether to replace files, answer Y for yes.

archives-extract-done.text: A new supplies folder appeared, and the zip file is still there too.

archives-finale.text: Lesson two complete. You're ready for the tests. Start with test one, then take on the vault.

archives-find.text: First, go to your Downloads folder and see what arrived.

archives-find-done.text: Two zip files. A zip archive packs lots of files into one, like a parcel.

archives-locked.text: Go back to Downloads and unzip the locked parcel. When it asks for the password, type it and press Enter. You won't see it as you type. That's normal on Linux.

archives-locked-done.text: Unlocked. A wrong password would simply change nothing, so you can always try again.

archives-manifest.text: The parcel came with a manifest. Read it.

archives-manifest-done.text: The second parcel is locked, and the password is on a hidden sticky note on your Desktop.

archives-note.text: The locked parcel unpacked a new folder. Read what is inside.

archives-note-done.text: Both parcels delivered. You can now open any zip file, even a locked one.

archives-peek.text: Before opening a parcel, check what's inside. Type unzip, space, dash L, then the file name. Dash L means list.

archives-peek-done.text: Now you know what is inside, and nothing has been unpacked yet.

archives-sticky.text: Go to your Desktop and find the hidden sticky note. Remember, hidden files need L S dash A.

archives-sticky-done.text: The password is lantern. Remember it.

exploring-brief.text: Welcome, rookie. You've just entered an unfamiliar Linux machine, and the terminal is your only tool. Let's explore it together.

exploring-cat.text: Let's read the note. Type cat, then the file name: notes dot T X T. Cat prints what's inside a file.

exploring-cat-done.text: That is what the note says. Press Escape whenever you want to close it.

exploring-cat-message.text: There's a message in here. Read it.

exploring-cat-message-done.text: You found it. You just explored a Linux machine using nothing but the keyboard. Well done.

exploring-cd.text: Let's go inside Documents. Type C D, then a space, then Documents. C D means change directory.

exploring-cd-done.text: You're inside Documents now. Look at the prompt: it shows where you are.

exploring-cd-hidden.text: You found a hidden folder. Go inside it. You already know how.

exploring-cd-hidden-done.text: Hidden folders work like any other. The dot is just part of the name.

exploring-cd-up.text: Time to go back. Type C D, a space, and two dots. Two dots always mean one level up.

exploring-cd-up-done.text: You're back home. Keep climbing with C D dot dot and you'd reach the root, a single slash: the top of the whole machine.

exploring-finale.text: Lesson one complete. Next, lesson two teaches you how to open zip files, even locked ones.

exploring-ls.text: Now, what's around you? Type L S, short for list, to see what's in this place.

exploring-ls-a.text: Something here is hidden. Type L S, space, dash A. The A means all, so hidden things show up too.

exploring-ls-a-done.text: There it is: dot hidden. Names that start with a dot are hidden from a normal listing. They're not locked, just out of sight.

exploring-ls-docs.text: You're somewhere new. What's in here? Use the command you already know.

exploring-ls-docs-done.text: A text file and another folder. L S always lists the place you are standing in.

exploring-ls-done.text: Three folders appeared. In Linux, folders are called directories.

exploring-pwd.text: First question: where are you? Type P W D. It stands for print working directory, and it tells you exactly where you are.

exploring-pwd-done.text: That's your location. Every command you type runs from here.

unfamiliar-brief.text: This is your first test. A brand new machine, and no instructions. Somewhere inside is a hidden message. Find it.

unfamiliar-success.text: Message found. You did it without a guide. Nicely done.

vault-brief.text: Agent, this is the ultimate test. A locked vault. Its password was split into three parts, and each part is hidden in a file you will not see with a normal listing. Follow the clues, find all three parts, and open the vault. Good luck.

vault-part1.text: Part one found. Two to go.

vault-part3.text: Part three found. You have the whole password. Now open the vault.

vault-success.text: Vault open. Clearance granted. Go inside top secret and read everything.
